overview: Airport Stand and Gate Allocation addresses resource allocation is planned in silos, producing avoidable delays and occasionally infeasible instructions in aviation and airports operations. The first proof of value uses flight schedule, wing-span constraints and stand status. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is stand conflict incidents, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: flight schedule, wing-span constraints and stand status; define stand conflict incidents and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Airport COO / Airline Operations Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including replay disruption and edge cases with hard constraints enforced.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
